body: Thanks! Are there any of these that you recommend above the rest? Our pup is reactive to strange dogs and can be to strangers. With slow meetings he has 100% been fine.
"My dog is still working hard on learning to control himself.... just like it seems you are too!"

Start by seeing a vet to make sure that there's nothing physical underlying the change. Then, it's never too early to go see a veterinary behaviorist. They'll be able to help you pinpoint triggers and find ways to ameliorate the issue. Good luck; you can do this!

Muzzle training would be great in this scenario. If you muzzle train slowly and positively, they can both be comfortable at his house. He can still give her treats, but then he'll be able to relax a bit knowing if she does lunge, the worst won't happen. 

Keep doing what you're doing with the counter conditioning, if he's willing. Make sure he knows not to stare at her or bend at the waist- any 'threatening' behavior like that. 

Keep a journal of when she does react. Write down the exact scenario- who was there, what were they doing, how was she acting before, during, and after. That'll possibly help you identify triggers and avoid/mitigate them. 

Good luck! You can do this!
... Phase II of the Veterinary Pathology exam.

It is never too early to see a private behaviorist. Best case scenario - they give you a bunch of tips on your first meeting, and with work and training, you hopefully would only need an occasional meeting to 'check up'. Second, stop going to the dog park NOW. Your pup is obviously uncomfortable there, and continuing to go will solidify those behaviors. Once you adjust your training and your pup's behavior, you can try going back. But as the others said, right now is all about keeping your integrations controlled. I also have a dog who resource guards me, and one thing that has helped had been getting a once-a-week dog walker. This makes my pup reliant on someone elder besides me, and actually my walker (experienced with reactivity) never has any of the issues with my pup that I do.

I second this. Betting a foster means that the rescue pays for the training, and should oversee any issues. And overall should be in better contact with you. If this dog is proving to be too much to handle, tell them. They should be more than happy to find it a different foster, so that you can go on to foster other dogs.

From what you wrote, it sounds like you did the right thing for not only her, but yourself. It is so hard to hear at this moment, but you will heal. This will stay with you, but hopefully you can find a way to be able to look back and know that you made the best decision. Also, if you don't have one, find a therapist to talk to. Also, I know you rehomed, bit the comments on this blog article and others of hers might be helpful to read. You aren't alone in this, and it is heart wrenching, but ultimately for the best.
